label: early-episode a2 commitment (D1/GO before choosing a2, trials ~3-30)
explanation: Fires only at D1 and GO (never at D2, never when a state or action input is present), almost exclusively when the upcoming choice is a2 (99.9% of mass) and the previous choice was also a2 (stays; switches carry ~0.1%). It is confined to the early part of the episode: rate 4-5% in trials 3-19, falling to ~0 by trial 40 and silent on trials 0-2 and 50-99. At GO it comes with a strongly negative policy logit (choice < -8.9, confident a2), and it is enriched when S2 started out good (start_high=0, 88% of mass) and after a rewarded previous trial (91% of mass). The recorded predicate uses action, which at D1/GO is the agent own upcoming choice (legitimate to compute); since stays dominate, prev_action==2 is the observed proxy. Within a window, activation tends to be largest on the first a2 trials and to decay over consecutive a2 trials. It covers ~95% of activation mass, but precision is only ~10%: the unit is silent on most early a2 D1/GO steps, and I found no observed variable (streak length within the window, reward history, transition, good state) that separates active from inactive episodes (active in only ~46% of episodes). Narrowing to start_high=0 and trials 3-19 raises precision to 0.16 but loses 30% of the mass. Most likely it tracks a slow, episode-specific drift of the early-episode a2 bias rather than a crisp task event.
